extracted.intended_audience: news website publishers, journalists, NewsGuard readers, and organizations seeking or challenging NewsGuard ratings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how NewsGuard reviews and updates website credibility ratings, including regular reviews, immediate re-reviews triggered by notable events, and publisher/reader requests for reassessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular review of each website's rating
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard’s team reviews each website’s rating regularly to ensure accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a rating is published, the team regularly reviews it to account for any changes in the site’s credibility or transparency practices that might affect NewsGuard’s nine journalistic criteria or the site’s overall rating. In some checks, the rating and Nutrition Label may remain unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduled review vs. immediate re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratings are reviewed on a routine schedule but may be re-reviewed immediately when notable changes occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If something notable changes, NewsGuard may review a website’s rating immediately rather than waiting for its regularly scheduled update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership or leadership change as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in the site's ownership or leadership triggers an immediate review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists 'The site’s ownership or leadership changes' as a circumstance prompting an immediate update of the site's rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major journalism award as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: Winning a major award for journalism prompts an immediate rating review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard will update sites immediately if 'The site wins a major award for its journalism.' This is treated as a notable change that can affect credibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-profile original content as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing a high-profile piece of content prompts an immediate review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An immediate update may occur if 'The site publishes a high-profile piece of content,' since such content can affect judgments about accuracy, editorial standards, and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-profile error or controversy as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-profile error or involvement in controversy triggers immediate reassessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard updates sites immediately if 'The site makes a high-profile error or is involved in a controversy,' as this may change adherence to journalistic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in misinformation alert monitoring as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: A previously reliable site appearing in misinformation monitoring alerts prompts immediate review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'A previously reliable site appears in one of our alerts monitoring common misinformation narratives,' NewsGuard may re-review the rating immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: New domain with same content as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: Launching a new domain that republishes the same content prompts an immediate review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard will update ratings immediately if 'A site launches a new domain with the same content,' since domain proliferation can affect transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive changes to practices as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: When a site changes practices to better adhere to the nine criteria (e.g., disclosing ownership or instituting a corrections policy), NewsGuard may re-review and update the rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: disclosing ownership or instituting a corrections policy. Publishers who make such changes can contact NewsGuard to request a new review once changes are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of errors in NewsGuard's reporting as trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: If NewsGuard becomes aware of an error or inaccuracy in its own reporting, it will re-review the affected rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such awareness can come through a report from a user or publisher; NewsGuard treats this as grounds for immediate review and correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nine journalistic criteria (central rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard evaluates sites according to its 'nine journalistic criteria' which determine adherence to credibility and transparency standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly references the nine criteria as the substantive standards that drive ratings; publishers are directed to review these criteria to improve ratings. (The nine criteria themselves are referenced but not enumerated on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition Label updates and editor's note disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When a site's rating or Nutrition Label is changed, the change is documented in an editor’s note on the site’s NewsGuard page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a site’s rating changes due to adherence change to one of the nine criteria, or if its Nutrition Label is updated, the changes are 'noted in an editor’s note at the bottom of the page.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for readers/publishers to request review or report errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers or publishers who believe a rating contains factual errors can contact NewsGuard to request review; publishers can contact the team after making corrective changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page contains links labeled 'contact our team' for both readers and publishers and instructs publishers to review the nine criteria and then notify NewsGuard to conduct a new review after making changes.
